_comment: Fastest full clears -- all five rounds of a map, no exceptions. A partial clear is not a time, and the board never shows one. Times are the server's own round clock, summed across the five rounds; nothing here comes from a client.

store._devSuffix: Dev runs write to a separate set of keys so testing with infinite money and skipped rounds can never touch the real board. Shared/Dev decides which is used.

display._pages: The board cycles: one page per map, then a personal-bests page. Cycling rather than paging by input means the board is readable while you walk past it, which is the only way anyone will ever read it.

validation._note: A leaderboard is the one place in this game where a bad number is permanent, so submissions are gated hard. Anything rejected is logged with its reason rather than silently dropped.
validation._requireEliminations: A five-round clear eliminates exactly 2+3+4+5+6 = 20 bots. If the elimination count does not match the schedule the run did not happen the way the time claims it did, and it is refused.

tierWeighting._note: Times are NOT normalised by tier. A rec-tier clear and a pro-tier clear sit on the same board and the tier is shown next to the name -- because the interesting question is not 'who is fastest' but 'who was fastest against what'. Sorting by adjusted time would hide exactly the thing worth seeing.

personal._note: The player's own bests are kept in their profile as well as on the board, so the goal you are actually chasing is visible without a DataStore round trip.
